In America there are federal and state laws. There are no federal laws that regulate snow tires so all legislation is done at the state level. The standard state law for snow tires will read like "studded tires or tire chains are permitted from November 1st through May 1st" or some variation of that. Now, for the states that experience heavy snow in the winter the only significant variation in snow tire laws are in the states that have mountain ranges. For example, Colorado requires commercial trucks to carry chains during the winter to put on during heavy snow.
Cities sometimes ban the use of chains though, so it gets even more complicated than just federal and state.
